name: Job Forge - AI-Powered Resume Optimization and Job Tracking Platform
description: A web tool that helps users tailor resumes to job postings by analyzing job descriptions with AI, providing personalized recommendations, and enabling job application tracking through a dashboard.

hero.title: Job Forge
hero.subtitle: A full-stack web app that helps job seekers tailor resumes, discover jobs, and track applications using real-time AI feedback and NLP-driven match scores.
hero.tools: React, Flask, SQLite, OpenAI API, Indeed API, Tailwind CSS, CORS

overview.description: Job Forge is a web-based platform designed to simplify the job search by unifying three critical tasks into one place: resume optimization, real-time job matching, and application tracking. Built with job seekers in mind, the platform allows users to upload resumes, search jobs through the Indeed API, and instantly receive AI-powered feedback on how well their resumes align with each posting. Suggestions for improvement help applicants tailor content to pass applicant tracking systems (ATS), while a centralized dashboard keeps saved jobs and progress organized.
overview.description2: We designed Job Forge to address the frustrations of today’s job market, where candidates often juggle multiple platforms, repetitive resume edits, and impersonal hiring filters. Inspired by tools like Grammarly, the interface emphasizes clarity and usability, while the backend leverages NLP and vector similarity scoring to generate meaningful insights. The result is a tool that empowers job seekers to apply strategically rather than blindly, giving them a stronger chance of breaking through automated filters and landing interviews.
overview.challenge: Job seekers face fragmented and frustrating experiences: they bounce between job boards, rewrite their resumes repeatedly, and often get filtered out by applicant tracking systems (ATS) before a human ever reviews their application. The process is inefficient, impersonal, and discouraging.
overview.goal: Design an integrated platform that empowers users to manage their job search in one place by optimizing resumes with AI-driven feedback, surfacing relevant job postings, and tracking applications so candidates can apply with confidence and increase their chances of breaking through automated filters.

stat1.findings: Job Search Fatigue and Emotional Burnout Are Widespread
stat1.evidence: Honestly, I’m exhausted. I’ve been sending out dozens of applications every week and half of them don’t even get a reply. It feels like I’m just shouting into a void. After a while, you start to feel stuck and even question your worth.
stat1.relevance: Emotional burnout and ghosting are happening widely, and clear status updates with progress tracking are needed to reduce frustration.

stat2.findings: Interview Processes Are Often Unfair and Anxious
stat2.evidence: I had to go through three different rounds of interviews for one job, and no one ever told me how long the process would take. It made me so anxious. Even worse, the system they used to send updates wouldn't appear in my inbox, so I was left in the dark. I just wanted clear, honest communication.
stat2.relevance: Prolonged, unclear interviews and poor communication are happening, and structured timelines with transparent updates are needed to ease anxiety.

stat3.findings: Qualified candidates are often screened out or ignored by automated systems
stat3.evidence: I applied to over 100 jobs in six months, and most of the time I never even made it past the first filter. It’s hard not to feel like the system is broken when you never get a fair shot at showing your skills.
stat3.relevance: Over-reliance on automated filters and vague rejection criteria leads to qualified applicants being dismissed prematurely.

stat1.findings: Job Applications Are Too Long and Complicated
stat1.evidence: Over 53% of survey respondents flagged “unnecessarily long applications” as the most frustrating part of the job hunt, with writing cover letters (17%) and constantly updating resumes (14%) not far behind
stat1.relevance: Streamlined application flows such as resume re-use, summarized job details, and autofill are needed to reduce friction and prevent abandonment.

stat2.evidence: 65% of candidates report not receiving reliable communication during the hiring process. Many wait 1–2+ months for updates, and over a third get no acknowledgment at all. Nearly half (47%) said that poor communication would make them drop out of the hiring process entirely
stat2.relevance: Reliable communication systems like automated status updates, in-app messaging, or acknowledgment templates are needed to assure candidates and prevent dropout.

stat3.findings: Candidates struggle to understand why applications fail
stat3.evidence: 46% of job seekers report athey never received feedback after submitting resumes. They don’t know if the issue was with formatting, missing skills, or poor alignment with the job description.
stat3.relevance: Providing actionable feedback on resumes and applications helps users improve future submissions, reduces frustration, and makes the job search feel more manageable.

stat1.findings: Existing tools specialize but don’t integrate
stat1.evidence: Tools like Jobscan or Resumeworded provide scores but often fail to explain why certain matches are weak or how to improve effectively. Users may feel “gamed” by vague keyword scoring, leading to frustration or mistrust.
stat1.relevance: Job seekers juggle multiple platforms, creating friction and inefficiency.

stat2.findings: Current resume optimizers lack transparency and usability
stat2.evidence: Jobscan focuses solely on keyword matching for resumes but doesn’t handle job discovery or application tracking. While LinkedIn Jobs and Indeed surface postings but offer limited resume feedback—users still have to tailor resumes manually.
stat2.relevance: A need for delivering clear, explainable AI suggestions rather than opaque scores.

stat3.evidence: LinkedIn Jobs and Indeed allow bookmarking or saving jobs, but neither provides a holistic dashboard to track applications across platforms.
stat3.relevance: Candidates end up using spreadsheets, notes apps, or memory to follow their progress. This adds stress and makes it harder to apply strategically.

phase1.process: In examining the problem space, the team approached the job search experience as a system with recurring inefficiencies and structural gaps. Pain points such as the time-consuming nature of resume rewriting, the lack of feedback following rejections, and the fragmentation of job boards (pink/red notes) were systematically mapped to opportunities (yellow notes) like creating a centralized hub, visualizing progress, and clarifying ATS processes. These opportunities were then translated into concrete feature concepts (green notes), including AI-driven resume scoring, a Kanban-style application tracker, and motivational prompts. Research insights and user quotes (blue notes) reinforced the validity of this framing, revealing a consistent sense of frustration and uncertainty across job seekers. This structured synthesis enabled the team to reconceptualize the problem not as a collection of individual user complaints, but as evidence of broader inefficiencies within the hiring ecosystem—inefficiencies that Job Forge was strategically designed to address.

phase1.summary: From the beginning, our UI decisions were guided by clarity and ease of use, drawing inspiration from tools like Grammarly that balance clean layouts with actionable feedback. Early prototypes explored a sidebar navigation paired with a dashboard-style layout, ensuring users could move smoothly between uploading resumes, searching jobs, and reviewing scores. Through peer feedback, we prioritized simplicity in navigation, refining the interface toward a card-based job search design and a streamlined dashboard for saved jobs and resume scores. One of the major design pivots came from our attempt to integrate direct in-app PDF editing. While conceptually appealing, it quickly became clear that editing resumes directly in the browser was both technically complex given our timeline and confusing for users in practice. Instead, we shifted to a cleaner solution: providing actionable suggestions that users could apply in their own documents before re-uploading. These iterations reinforced our focus on readability, quick navigation, and immediate feedback, resulting in a UI that supported the natural job seeker workflow: uploading resumes, evaluating alignment, making improvements, and applying with confidence.
phase1.caption: Early attempt at in-browser PDF editing — ultimately too cluttered for users and technically unfeasible within our timeline, leading us to pivot toward a cleaner suggestion-based approach.

phase2.summary: The user flow is designed to guide applicants seamlessly from start to finish. After a quick login or registration, users land on a dashboard that keeps everything organized. They can upload a resume, then search and save jobs pulled in real time from Indeed. For each role, Job Forge instantly generates a resume score, showing how well their resume aligns with the job description. Users then receive actionable suggestions—both general improvements and job-specific tailoring tips—to refine their resume. By iterating and re-uploading, applicants can track progress and boost their chances before moving on to apply with confidence.

reflection.learned: We learned that building a strong product means balancing clarity, feasibility, and iteration. Attempting complex features like in-browser PDF editing showed us how easily usability and development constraints can collide. By listening to peer feedback and refining our approach, we discovered that a simpler, suggestion-based workflow not only made the product more intuitive but also aligned better with what job seekers truly needed.
reflection.improvements: With more time and resources, we would refine resume parsing and suggestion accuracy, ensuring that feedback feels both precise and actionable for a wide range of job seekers. We would also expand usability testing beyond peers to include a broader audience with diverse backgrounds and career goals, surfacing deeper insights into different user needs. Together, these improvements would strengthen the product by creating a smoother experience across varied job search journeys.
reflection.future: Looking ahead, we see opportunities to integrate real-time editing support directly into the resume review process, giving users instant feedback as they refine their documents. We also envision expanding job board integrations beyond Indeed, allowing job seekers to centralize their search within one platform. These steps would transform Job Forge into an even more comprehensive and empowering tool for applicants.
